certainty_reasoning: What survives is one clause of admiration in a letter to Robert Ross - 'I met one beautiful person, called André, with wonderful eyes' - with no approach, no second meeting and no outcome. That is admiration recorded by Wilde and nothing more, so attraction-expressed with outcome 'unknown' is the only class the page supports: romantic-nonsexual would assert a mutual connection the letter does not document, and documented-sexual has no first-person statement behind it. Candour about the bar: this is the thinnest item in the exile-liaison tier. The README requires that desire be legible as desire to a reader who does not hold the coding hypothesis, and a bare 'one beautiful person … with wonderful eyes' sits at or just under that line; the reading that this is desire rather than aesthetic notice is this project's, not a scholarly source's, and a later check may reasonably prefer to keep André as a bio record with no edge. Note also that the following sentence's stronger declaration - 'One would have followed him into the desert' - attaches to Pietro, not to André, and is not borrowed here. Standing caveat for this tier: the record is one-sided by nature. These men left no papers; everything known is what Wilde wrote to a friend. An unrecorded outcome is not evidence of no outcome, and André's own view of the meeting is not recorded anywhere.
date_label: Met on a three-day trip to Nice with Harold Mellor, reported in a letter the editors date Thursday [? 12 January 1899] from Napoule.
summary: During his Riviera winter of 1898-99, Wilde crossed from Napoule to Nice for three days with Harold Mellor and wrote to Robert Ross that he had met a beautiful person named André, with wonderful eyes. That single clause is the whole of the record: no surname, no age, no occupation, no second mention anywhere in the correspondence read, and no indication of what if anything followed.

sources.quote: I have been over again to Nice with Harold Mellor, for three days. It was most pretty and gay, and music everywhere. I met one beautiful person, called André, with wonderful eyes, and a little Italian, Pietro, like a young St John. One would have followed him into the desert.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, Thursday [? 12 January 1899], Napoule - reporting the Nice excursion. The final sentence's 'him' refers to Pietro, the immediately preceding name.
sources.supports: The whole of the record for André: a named person met at Nice, described as beautiful and with wonderful eyes, with no outcome recorded
